data.title: Crisaborole 2% ointment
data.summary: IX Immunomodulators · Topical phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) inhibitor (boron-containing benzoxaborole)
data.body:
_Topicals · IX Immunomodulators_

**Class:** Topical phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) inhibitor (boron-containing benzoxaborole)

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits PDE4 → increases intracellular cAMP → reduces TNF-α, IL-12, IL-23 and other cytokines
- Small molecule with boron atom → good skin penetration; rapidly metabolised to inactive forms when absorbed

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Mild–moderate atopic dermatitis in patients aged 3 months and older (approved)
- Off-label: seborrhoeic dermatitis, psoriasis (intertriginous), vitiligo (limited)

## Dose & formulations
- Thin layer twice daily to affected areas

## Adverse effects
- Application-site burning or stinging (about 4%)
- Contact urticaria (rare)

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity

## Pregnancy & lactation
Minimal absorption; limited data.

## Viva points
- Non-steroidal, PDE4 → ↑cAMP
- Approved from 3 months of age
- Burning at application is the main complaint

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.18 (PDE4 inhibitors — crisaborole); Khopkar edition predates it. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
